what: hir-ty: a foreign function (in an `extern` block) without `safe` gets a safe fn signature; rustc's fn_sig makes it `unsafe`. `lower.rs` ~4399 builds FnSigKind safety from `data.is_unsafe()`, which hir-def sets only from a literal `unsafe` keyword (signatures.rs FunctionSignature::lower). It should be unsafe when the container is an ExternBlockId and the function is not `safe` (FnFlags::EXPLICIT_SAFE), as `is_fn_unsafe_to_call` already decides for calls. Seen in blaze-diagnostics: the fn item type of `extern "C" { fn printf(f: *const u8, ...) -> i32; }` prints without `unsafe` (tests::bodies::print::a_function_item_is_its_signature_and_its_path), and suspicious_runtime_symbol_definitions fires on a `pub unsafe extern "C" fn strlen(s: *const c_char) -> usize` that matches core's canonical declaration (tests::lints::names::items::runtime_symbols_matching_and_mangled), since the signatures compare unequal on safety. Also affects fn-pointer coercion of foreign fns (a safe `fn` pointer from an unsafe foreign fn must be an error).
